newsitem.title: MONACO: ATHLETICS-KOMEN HOPES TO END HISTORIC WEEK WITH ANOTHER RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN HOPES TO END HISTORIC WEEK WITH ANOTHER RECORD.

text.p: Kenyan world champion Daniel Komen attacks his own 3,000 metres world record at the Monaco Grand Prix on Saturday at the end of an historic week in middle and distance running.

After world records in the men's 800, 3,000 metres steeplechase and 5,000 in a remarkable few hours at Wednesday's Zurich Grand Prix, it would be a major achievement for Komen to better the 3,000 best of seven minutes 20.67 seconds set in Rieti, Italy, last season.

The Kenyan was involved in an intense 5,000 battle with Haile Gebrselassie in Zurich when the Ethiopian destroyed his own world record with a time of 12:41.86. Second-placed Komen set a Kenyan record of 12:44.90, close to the previous world mark.

But even in the Monte Carlo casinos where millionaires are prepared to spend an average person's yearly salary on a night of gambling, it would be a brave man who would bet against a 21-year-old athlete who first gained his endurance from running 20 kms to and from school as a child.

Before he went to Athens earlier this month to win the 5,000 world title, Komen set a world record for the two miles of 7:58.61 in Belgium. On the same track last season the Kenyan went within 0.05 seconds of the previous 3,000 best during an astonishing few weeks of running.

Denmark's former Kenyan Wilson Kipketer, who took nearly half a second off Seb Coe's 16-year-old 800 world record on Wednesday, the oldest record in the book, with a time of one minute 41.24 seconds, will also take part in Monaco.
But he is unlikely to be able to lift himself again so soon after Zurich's performance when he ran an astonishing 48.10 seconds for the first 400 metres.

In the 3,000 steeplechase world champion Wilson Boit Kipketer takes on compatriots Moses Kipatani and Bernard Barmasai who pulled him along to a world record of 7:59.08 seconds in Zurich. Again, another record three days later would be tough.
The men's 1,500 metres could also be fast with Olympic champion Morceli clashing with Spain's former Olympic champion Fermin Cacho, the silver medallist at last year's Olympic Games in Atlanta.
Cacho broke Briton Steve Cram's 12-year-old European record when he finished second in Zurich in 3:28.95 in Zurich.

American world 100 metres champions Maurice Greene and Marion Jones are both in action again against the athletes who defeated them in Zurich. Greene takes on Namibia's Frankie Fredericks over 100 while Jones runs the women's 200 against Jamaican veteran Merlene Ottey.

Ottey, one of the most popular athletes on the circuit, flew into nearby Nice from Zurich on an aircraft which boasted a glamorous set of passengers including nine times Olympic champion Carl Lewis and American singer Tina Turner.
